artifacts.interpretation: Documents the scale and reproducibility of the M5 evidence base (240 PHREEQC scenarios, 21,600 factorial fits, 160 field pairs) and shows that mean class-level recovery is consistently higher on richer ion panels across every comparator method.

artifacts.technical_description: Generated by r_figures/plot_m5_publication_figures.R (figure2_r_model_performance) from benchmark_fits.csv and phreeqc_inverse_baseline.csv.
artifacts.interpretation: Hydrosheaf Guarded sits on the favourable corner of the false-discovery-rate/equivalence-class-F1 frontier, but every sparse comparator, including Hydrosheaf Guarded, still carries a non-trivial false-discovery rate, and the conventional PHREEQC first-minimal baseline trails the sparse comparators on this frontier despite full thermodynamic consistency.

artifacts.caption: Exact reaction-equivalence classes and conditional evidence separation. (a) The three exact non-unique class pairs (calcium-sodium exchange/sodium-calcium exchange, magnesium-sodium exchange/sodium-magnesium exchange, and anorthite/calcite), each with two indistinguishable members under sparse major-ion chemistry. (b) Sparse-ion stoichiometric loadings explaining the collinearity: anorthite and calcite load identically on calcium and bicarbonate, the only ions either reaction affects that the 11-ion panel measures. (c) Mean evidence-lifted resolution index (ELRI) by class pair and measurement tier (0 = unresolved, 1 = resolved). (d) Fraction of scenarios in which the correct member of the anorthite/calcite pair was identified when that class was truly active, by measurement tier.
artifacts.technical_description: Generated by r_figures/plot_m5_publication_figures.R (figure3_r_equifinality_elri) from equivalence_classes.csv, tableS1_reaction_stoichiometry.csv, and data_tier_evidence_lifted_resolution.csv.
artifacts.interpretation: Sparse major-ion chemistry has exact stoichiometric non-uniqueness, including a mineralogically unrelated pair (anorthite/calcite) that a reader would not anticipate without seeing the stoichiometric loadings; additional diagnostics separate the two exchange pairs far more effectively than the anorthite/calcite pair, and discrimination of the latter does not improve monotonically with more diagnostics.

artifacts.caption: Data-tier (core/plus-lite/enhanced) recovery and evidence-lifted resolution. (a) Equivalence-class F1 by tier (boxplots; white dot = mean). (b) False-discovery rate by tier. (c) Evidence-lifted resolution index (ELRI) by tier. (d) Reaction-level Hydrosheaf-Core evidence-gate scores by reaction and tier. Boxes show the interquartile range with whiskers to 1.5x IQR and outlying points shown individually.
artifacts.technical_description: Generated by r_figures/plot_m5_publication_figures.R (figure4_r_data_tiers) from data_tier_experiment.csv, data_tier_evidence_lifted_resolution.csv, and tableS15_data_tier_reaction_evidence.csv.
artifacts.interpretation: Moving from the core to the enhanced diagnostic tier produces only a modest gain in mean class F1 and false-discovery rate but a larger gain in evidence-gate scores for several reactions, indicating that additional diagnostics mainly help an analyst choose among already-identified alternatives rather than expanding which scenarios are correctly classified at all. Ion-ablation, held-out-ion falsification, and next-best-measurement results are reported in Supplementary Figures S8 and S9, not in this figure.

artifacts.technical_description: Generated by r_figures/plot_m5_publication_figures.R (figure6_r_field_transfer) from ghana_field_pairs.csv, external_field_evidence_lifted_resolution.csv, and tableS17_external_field_evidence_lifted_resolution.csv.
artifacts.interpretation: Ghana and external field datasets are plausibility/transfer audits of the identifiability framework, not independent reaction-truth validation; external ELRI values are consistently low, and the anorthite/calcite pair remains essentially unresolved (ELRI near zero) across all three field datasets and both available tiers, mirroring the synthetic-benchmark result in Figure 3.

artifacts.caption: Comparative performance of seven inverse methods at 3% analytical noise with the full 11-ion panel, with 95% confidence intervals, convergence rate, and median runtime per fit. The asterisk marks the conventional PHREEQC inverse row (first-minimal model), which aggregates across the strict 5% and relaxed 20% uncertainty settings rather than a single noise level, unlike the other six rows, and has no reconstruction-RMSE or runtime entry because it is not solved by the same coordinate-descent pipeline.
artifacts.technical_description: Generated by scripts/make_m5_publication_tables.py from benchmark_fits.csv and phreeqc_inverse_baseline.csv.
artifacts.interpretation: Hydrosheaf Guarded achieves the lowest false-discovery rate among sparse comparators; the conventional PHREEQC baseline's first-minimal-model recovery is lower than every guarded comparator despite full thermodynamic consistency. Hydrosheaf Guarded and Thermodynamic Elastic Net share identical extent RMSE, reconstruction RMSE, and runtime because Hydrosheaf Guarded reuses the same coordinate-descent solve and differs only in the applied support threshold.
